077.t: Testing: Normal, Boundary and Invalid Data
o: Choose suitable data and explain iterative and final testing.
Apply this to another software scenario.

c: Representative valid inputs normally expected during use. Consider this in a test a marks form.
Values at, immediately below and immediately above an allowed limit. Consider this in a ticket quantity checker.
Inputs rejected by the required rules, including out-of-range or wrong-format data. Consider this in a age-restricted service.
Iterative testing runs during development; terminal testing checks the finished solution. Consider this in a sports score input.
